items.title: Kent Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: They probably look at me like I’m really crazy but you know I tell people all the time if Mozart or Brahms or Beethoven or those guys were alive they wouldn’t be doing that.

ctx.x: You’re playing that again? I wrote that 300 years ago, come on. You know? What’s happening? And I don’t think classical musicians would understand that. They probably look at me like I’m really crazy but you know I tell people all the time if Mozart or Brahms or Beethoven or those guys were alive they wouldn’t be doing that. They’d probably be hanging out at some club, you know trying to, yeah, “I might learn how to swing. Really? Yeah, let me check that out.” I’m just saying I mean it would be what’s ever is the…
music wasn’t really being played every night the way it’s being played now. You know so think about that. That’s kind of strange.
